## Verdict: APPROVE with notes (no finding or checklist failure at or above the critical threshold; suggestions and one inconclusive item remain)

The pull request is ready to merge: every acceptance criterion passed verification, and what remains are minor wording and test-coverage suggestions.
Rule applied: rule 6 — findings and checklist failures below the threshold, plus one INCONCLUSIVE item → APPROVE with notes

## Code Review Findings

### 🟡 Suggestion / Minor (6)

<details><summary>6 items</summary>

1. `src/sqllens/agent/tools/run_sql.py` lines 73-78: `RunSqlTool.execute` classifies the statement with `first_sql_keyword` and `is_read_shaped` after the runner has already executed it. A tokenizer exception other than `TokenError` then lands in the tool's broad `except` and is reported as "Error executing query", although the statement ran. The built-in runners classify first, so only a custom runner that commits before classifying can reach this. (raised by 1/4 agents)
2. `src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py` lines 48-49: the `first_sql_keyword` docstring says comments and opening parentheses are skipped "as that dialect's tokenizer skips them". The tokenizer only drops comments; the function's own loop skips the `L_PAREN` tokens. (raised by 1/4 agents) <!-- inertness: first-conjunct=held limb-one=held limb-two=held; evidence: the subject is the docstring sentence only, no mechanism coverage is disputed and correcting it changes no output; searched .sh/.py/.jq/.yml consumers, CLAUDE.md and the prompt extensions for a reader of this docstring and found none; the docstring is in a source file the program never prints -->
3. `src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py` lines 142-172 (`_cte_reference_ids`): no test covers a CTE that shares a catalog table's name and reads that table in its own body, such as `WITH pg_class AS (SELECT * FROM pg_class) SELECT * FROM pg_class` on Postgres. Correct behavior depends on how sqlglot's `traverse_scope` fills `cte_sources` for a CTE body, which is AST behavior CLAUDE.md says needs a test. (raised by 1/4 agents)
- VC-50: FAIL (suggestion) — The tools.md query_type bullet asserts query_type is the leading keyword found by sqlglot's tokenizer for the configured dialect, skipping comments and opening parentheses, and is "" when no keyword leads the statement (first token a string, number, quoted identifier or symbol, no token left, or SQL the tokenizer rejects). [docs/internal/mcp-server/tools.md:302]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  tools.md:302 says query_type is "" when no keyword leads the statement. first_sql_keyword (src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py:77-78) returns token.text.upper() for any TokenType.VAR token, i.e. an unquoted non-keyword identifier. Input `foo bar` (an agent can emit it; it is only rejected later by the DB) has no leading keyword, yet query_type is "FOO", not "". The function's own docstring (lines 50-51) says 'a keyword or an unquoted identifier', so the doc's absolute 'when no keyword leads' omits this case. The rest of the claim (comments/paren skipping, string/number/quoted identifier/symbol -> "", empty -> "", TokenError -> "") matches lines 68-85. Consequence is small, since the doc's list is introduced by 'for example' and the identifier case is rare in practice.

  </details>

- VC-52: FAIL (suggestion) — The transport.md bullet says RunSqlTool.execute writes the result CSV when a statement `is_read_shaped` under the configured dialect classifies as read-shaped returns rows; the doc covers that condition only, while the code also writes the CSV when the runner's frame carries READ_RESULT_ATTR. [docs/internal/mcp-server/transport.md:125]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  INVALID answer stored FAIL (claim_provenance source_authored): run_sql.py:78 guards the branch (including the write_file call at 129-131) with `is_read_shaped(args.sql, self.dialect) or df.attrs.get(READ_RESULT_ATTR)`, so the code does also write the CSV for a runner-marked frame. transport.md:125 says 'When a read-shaped statement (is_read_shaped ...) returns rows, RunSqlTool.execute writes the result CSV'. That sufficient-condition statement is true as written and does not say 'only when'; the extra READ_RESULT_ATTR path is a documented-elsewhere contract (read-only-safety.md:124) and is a bullet about event-loop blocking, not a trigger spec. No unchanged source requires transport.md to enumerate every trigger, so no counterexample to the authored text exists. The claim's description of the code is accurate, but it adds an exhaustiveness property the doc does not assert.

  </details>

- VC-54: FAIL (suggestion) — The is_read_shaped docstring asserts it is a cheap first-token check used by SQL runners, and that the ReadOnlyGuardRunner (when enabled) has already enforced the whole statement is read-only; RunSqlTool.execute now also calls it, and first_sql_keyword tokenizes the whole statement. [src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py:91]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  readonly.py:68-85: first_sql_keyword calls resolved.tokenize(sql) on the whole statement, so it is not a first-token scan; a TokenError anywhere (e.g. unterminated string late in the statement) returns "" and is_read_shaped is False (readonly.py:70-71, 96). The is_read_shaped docstring (lines 91-94) calls it a 'Cheap first-token check' and says it is used by SQL runners. Callers (grep): mysql/postgres/sqlite sql_runner.py (141/171/152) and agent/tools/run_sql.py:78, RunSqlTool.execute, which is a tool, not a runner, and which runs it whether or not ReadOnlyGuardRunner is enabled. So the docstring is stale: it omits the RunSqlTool caller and mislabels whole-statement tokenization as a first-token check. Low impact, wording only.

  </details>

</details>

The repo has no MySQL or SQLite test showing that a comment ends at the first `*/`. The tests at 1284-1348 use nested markers but do not establish the NESTED_COMMENTS values. Missing evidence: the installed sqlglot 30.22 source for the Postgres, MySQL and SQLite tokenizers, or a run of first_sql_keyword on `/* a /* b */ c */ SELECT 1` under each dialect. I did not run that.

acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `first_sql_keyword` returns `SELECT` for a `SELECT` preceded by any mix of leading whitespace, opening parentheses, `--` comment lines and `/* … */` comments (at minimum `-- note` + newline + `SELECT 1`, `/* note */ SELECT 1`, `/* a */ (SELECT 1)`, `( -- a` + newline + `SELECT 1)`) and for a keyword touching a symbol (at minimum `SELECT*FROM t`, `SELECT/* c */1`), with no dialect and with each of `sqlite`, `postgres` and `mysql`; it returns `WITH` for the same prefixes before a `WITH` query; and every existing `TestFirstSqlKeyword` case keeps its expected value.
- [ ] `first_sql_keyword("/* a /* b */ c */ SELECT 1", "postgres")` returns `SELECT`, and with `mysql` or `sqlite` it returns `C`, matching how each engine ends the comment.
- [ ] `first_sql_keyword("# c\nSELECT 1", "mysql")` returns `SELECT`; with `postgres`, `sqlite` or no dialect it returns `""`.
- [ ] `first_sql_keyword` returns `""` for, at minimum, the SQL texts `'x' AS a`, `1 AS a` and `"t"` (a quoted identifier), each with `postgres`, and for empty and whitespace-only SQL; and `first_sql_keyword(sql, "no-such-dialect")` equals `first_sql_keyword(sql)` for every input this criterion and the three above name.
- [ ] `first_sql_keyword` returns `""` for a statement sqlglot's tokenizer cannot tokenize, with no dialect and with each of `sqlite`, `postgres` and `mysql` (at minimum `-- c\nSELECT 'x` and `/* unterminated SELECT 1`), and a unit test pins that result; an exception from the tokenizer other than `TokenError` propagates; `first_sql_keyword` uses only sqlglot's public API; and `src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py` contains no `_strip_leading_comments` and no regex, `.split()` or `startswith` test on SQL text in `first_sql_keyword`.
- [ ] `is_read_shaped("SELECT n FROM widgets # x\r'\n", "mysql")` is `True`, and `assert_select_only` accepts that statement with `dialect="mysql"`.
- [ ] Every existing `is_introspection_query` test keeps its expected value except the three unterminated comment-led `SHOW` cases of `test_own_engine_catalogs_detected` (`# tables\n/* again */ SHOW 'abc` and `/* c */ SHOW 'abc` on `mysql`, `-- c\nSHOW 'abc` on `postgres`), which now expect `False`, with a test comment saying that the read-only guard fails closed on the same input and the database rejects it, so it never returns rows; `is_introspection_query("#x\nSHOW 'abc", dialect="postgres")` is still `False`; and `is_introspection_query("# c\nSHOW TABLES")` with no dialect is `False`.
- [ ] `is_introspection_query` returns `False` for, at minimum, these data queries whose CTE name starts with a catalog prefix: `WITH pg_recent AS (SELECT 1 AS n) SELECT * FROM pg_recent` and `WITH PG_RECENT AS (SELECT 1 AS n) SELECT * FROM pg_recent` on `postgres`, and `WITH sqlite_recent AS (SELECT 1) SELECT * FROM sqlite_recent` on `sqlite`; and it still returns `True` for, at minimum, `WITH x AS (SELECT * FROM pg_class) SELECT * FROM x` and `WITH pg_recent AS (SELECT 1) SELECT * FROM pg_recent JOIN pg_class ON true` on `postgres`, `DESCRIBE information_schema.tables` on `mysql`, and `WITH sqlite_master AS (SELECT 1) SELECT * FROM sqlite_master, main.sqlite_master` on `sqlite`.
- [ ] When identifier normalization or scope analysis raises any exception, `is_introspection_query` excludes no node and logs the exception type: with `traverse_scope` patched to raise, `WITH pg_recent AS (SELECT 1) SELECT * FROM pg_recent` on `postgres` is `True`, and a unit test pins it.
- [ ] A comment-led `SELECT` and a `SELECT*FROM` read, each run through `SqliteRunner` over more rows than `max_rows`, return exactly `max_rows` rows of the selected columns, marked truncated, not a `rows_affected` frame; the MySQL runner, driven through a fake `pymysql`, executes `# c` + newline + `SELECT 1` on its `SSDictCursor` streaming cursor; and the Postgres runner, driven through a fake `psycopg2`, executes `-- c` + newline + `SELECT 1` on its named (server-side) cursor.
- [ ] The `run_sql` tool `build_agent` registers for a `mysql` URL classifies with the `mysql` dialect, and for a `sqlite` URL with the `sqlite` dialect.
- [ ] `RunSqlTool.execute` returns, for each of at minimum these statements, the result a plain `SELECT` returns — the CSV preview and `Results saved to file` line in `result_for_llm`, a `DataFrameComponent`, and `row_count`, `columns` and `results` metadata matching the returned rows — with `metadata["query_type"]` equal to the statement's leading keyword (`WITH`, `SELECT` or `SHOW`): a `WITH … SELECT` query, a `(SELECT …) UNION (SELECT …)` query, a `--`-led `SELECT`, a `/* */`-led `SELECT`, `SELECT*FROM widgets`, a `SHOW TABLES` statement, and, with the MySQL dialect, a `#`-led `SELECT`.
- [ ] A read-shaped statement that returns no rows (for example a `WITH` query whose filter matches nothing) gets `No rows returned`, with the truncation note when the row cap was hit, and never the `row(s) affected` message.
- [ ] A statement `is_read_shaped` does not classify as read-shaped (for example `UPDATE` with `read_only` off) still gets the `row(s) affected` notification and no result table.
- [ ] `RunSqlTool.execute` returns `success=False` for empty or whitespace-only SQL, with `read_only` on and off.
- [ ] `query_info["query_type"]` is `SELECT` for a `--`-led `SELECT`, and for a `#`-led `SELECT` when `components_to_blocks` is given `dialect="mysql"`.
- [ ] For a `run_sql` success card carrying a `WITH` data query's SQL (including one whose CTE name starts with a catalog prefix) followed by a multi-row `DataFrameComponent` of the kind `RunSqlTool` returns, `components_to_blocks` adds a user-visible table block; for a `SHOW TABLES` card followed by such a DataFrame, with `dialect="mysql"`, it adds no block.
- [ ] `pyproject.toml` requires `sqlglot>=30.22,<31`; no statement of the sqlglot version range in `src/`, `tests/`, `pyproject.toml`, `CLAUDE.md` or `docs/internal/` (other than the dated `docs/internal/production-readiness-v0.1.0.md`) gives a floor other than `30.22`; the read-only guard refers to `exp.Alter` directly; none of those files other than the dated `docs/internal/production-readiness-v0.1.0.md` mentions `_ALTER_TYPE` or `exp.AlterTable`; CLAUDE.md's sqlglot rule no longer names this issue, `first_sql_keyword`, `is_read_shaped` or `_strip_leading_comments` as open debt; and CLAUDE.md's `is_introspection_query` failure-path precedent states that an exception from identifier normalization or scope analysis excludes no CTE reference.
- [ ] The change leaves the runners' non-read-shaped branch as it is, so with `read_only` off a statement whose leading keyword is outside the read-shaped set, such as `EXPLAIN` or `VALUES`, and on Postgres `INSERT … RETURNING`, still gets the `row(s) affected` message (on SQLite, `INSERT … RETURNING` fails in that branch, as it does today); and with `read_only` off, a read sqlglot's tokenizer rejects but the engine runs — on SQLite, `SELECT n FROM widgets /* note` with no closing `*/` — gets `""` from `first_sql_keyword` and the `row(s) affected` message; and with `read_only` off, a data-modifying statement that starts with `WITH` (such as MySQL `WITH x AS (SELECT 1) UPDATE …`), with or without leading comments, takes the read-shaped branch as an uncommented one does today (on MySQL it is not committed; Postgres returns an error); #316 tracks that routing.
- [ ] Unit tests cover `RunSqlTool` with, at minimum, a `WITH` query, a leading-parenthesis set operation, a comment-led `SELECT` and a `SHOW` statement, and run without a live Postgres or MySQL server.

checklist.claim: The doc asserts that from 30.22 the three dialects' tokenizers treat nested block comments as their engines do: Postgres nests, MySQL and SQLite end a comment at the first `*/`.
checklist.source_excerpt: From 30.22 the three dialects' tokenizers also treat nested block comments as their engines do (Postgres nests; MySQL and SQLite end a comment at the first `*/`).

Grep of the head view for NESTED_COMMENTS finds nothing, and no sqlglot/dialects/mysql.py exists in the supplied artifacts, so sqlglot is a third-party dependency (pinned >=30.22,<31 at docs/internal/database-connectors/read-only-safety.md:46-52) whose source was not supplied. The repo tests only pin the Postgres half: tests/unit/test_safety.py:925 (`/* a /* b */ c */ SHOW TABLES`, postgres). checklist.claim: The tools.md query_type bullet asserts query_type is the leading keyword found by sqlglot's tokenizer for the configured dialect, skipping comments and opening parentheses, and is "" when no keyword leads the statement (first token a string, number, quoted identifier or symbol, no token left, or SQL the tokenizer rejects).
checklist.source_excerpt: It is `""` when no keyword leads the statement — for example a first token that is a string, number, quoted identifier or symbol, SQL with no token left after comments and parentheses, or SQL the tokenizer rejects.
checklist.verify_hint: Trace a statement whose first token is an unquoted non-keyword identifier (e.g. `foo bar`) through `first_sql_keyword` lines 73-85 (the `TokenType.VAR` branch); it returns the identifier uppercased, not "".
checklist.evidence: tools.md:302 says query_type is "" when no keyword leads the statement. first_sql_keyword (src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py:77-78) returns token.text.upper() for any TokenType.VAR token, i.e. an unquoted non-keyword identifier. Input `foo bar` (an agent can emit it; it is only rejected later by the DB) has no leading keyword, yet query_type is "FOO", not "". The function's own docstring (lines 50-51) says 'a keyword or an unquoted identifier', so the doc's absolute 'when no keyword leads' omits this case. The rest of the claim (comments/paren skipping, string/number/quoted identifier/symbol -> "", empty -> "", TokenError -> "") matches lines 68-85. Consequence is small, since the doc's list is introduced by 'for example' and the identifier case is rare in practice.

checklist.evidence: readonly.py:68-85: first_sql_keyword calls resolved.tokenize(sql) on the whole statement, so it is not a first-token scan; a TokenError anywhere (e.g. unterminated string late in the statement) returns "" and is_read_shaped is False (readonly.py:70-71, 96). The is_read_shaped docstring (lines 91-94) calls it a 'Cheap first-token check' and says it is used by SQL runners. Callers (grep): mysql/postgres/sqlite sql_runner.py (141/171/152) and agent/tools/run_sql.py:78, RunSqlTool.execute, which is a tool, not a runner, and which runs it whether or not ReadOnlyGuardRunner is enabled. So the docstring is stale: it omits the RunSqlTool caller and mislabels whole-statement tokenization as a first-token check. Low impact, wording only.
